SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
MONDAY - NOVEMBER 15, 2021 - 06:30 P.M.
CERRITOS SENIOR CENTER AT PAT NIXON PARK, MAJESTIC ROOM
12340 SOUTH STREET, CERRITOS, CA 90703
* COVID-19 NOTICE *
To protect public health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic and in compliance with the current Los Angeles County Health Officer Order and City of Cerritos COVID-19 Safety Plan, the Cerritos Senior Center at Pat Nixon Park, Majestic Room, will be open to the public thirty minutes prior to the meeting start time listed on this agenda. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20, N-29-20, and N-08-21, and subsequently by Assembly Bill 361 (Chapter 165, Statutes of 2021), this meeting may also be conducted via teleconference, if necessary. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting in-person at the Cerritos Senior Center at Pat Nixon Park, Majestic Room, subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL HELD MONDAY,
NOVEMBER 15, 2021, 6:30 P.M., CERRITOS SENIOR CENTER AT PAT NIXON PARK,
MAJESTIC ROOM, 12340 SOUTH STREET, CERRITOS, CA 90703

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 6:40 p.m.

2.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Grace Hu.

3.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council Member Bruce Barrows
  Council Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem Chuong Vo
  Mayor Grace Hu

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Hu, to excuse Council Member
  Naresh Solanki from the Monday, November 15, 2021, 6:30 p.m., City Council Special
  Meeting (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

4.  Review and consideration of the City of Cerritos City Charter (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer. A PowerPoint presentation
  was displayed.

  Councilmember Barrows reviewed the assessment provided by the Charter review
  subcommittee with regard to the proposed “update and modernization” version of the
  Charter as presented in the agenda report.

  Public comments were opened on the proposed “update and modernization” version of
  the Charter. Noting there were no members of the public who elected to provide public
  comments on this item, the public comments period was closed.

  Councilmember Barrows reviewed the proposed “anti-nepotism” policy inclusive of a
  definitions sections which results from public input on the draft document.

  Public comments were opened on the proposed “anti-nepotism” policy. Noting there
  were no members of the public who elected to provide public comments on this item,
  the public comments period was closed.

  Public comments were opened on City Council term limits and any other matter related
  to the City Charter.
 City of Cerritos  Monday, November 15, 2021, 6:30 p.m.
City Council Special Meeting  Page 2 of 4

4.  Review and consideration of the City of Cerritos City Charter (COUNCIL)
  (continued)

  Written correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  George Cottrell submitted written correspondence expressing concerns regarding
  unlimited terms of office for City Councilmembers.

  In-person comments:

  Martin Grossman requested clarification regarding the language of any proposed
  modifications to the City Council term limits provision in the Charter and stated the
  residents would like to see options regarding term limits ballot measures.

  Mel Cortez stated his support for the existing term limits provision, however, he would
  prefer a lifetime limit on the number a terms an individual may serve on the City
  Council.

  City Attorney Bill Ihrke affirmed that a ballot measure which is subject to the “simple
  majority” vote would require a fifty percent plus one (50% + 1) majority vote of those
  voting in that particular election for the measure to be successful. There can be
  “competing measures” however, each would be subject to the 50% + 1 majority vote to
  be successful.

  Jay Gray expressed his support for a lifetime limit of two full terms for City Council
  service and requested that various options for term limits ballot measures are placed
  before the voters.

  Sylvester Ani, Jr. expressed support for City Council term limits and inquired whether
  the City had considered shifting from an “at-large” to a “district” based format for City
  Council elections.

  Ram Kakkar inquired whether the Charter could include provisions to limit the benefits
  package received by elected officials.

  Sam Desai expressed support for a lifetime limit of two full terms for City Council service
  and for the proposed “anti-nepotism” policy.

  Elizabeth Mareira expressed support for “district” based voting in the City and inquired
  whether additional provisions could be included in the Charter to provide additional
  oversight of the City Manager.

  Gail Grossman expressed support to options for City Council term limit ballot measures
  and inquired whether there would be opportunities provided for members of the public
  to submit arguments and/or rebuttals.

  Bruce Leach expressed support for the current term limits provision.

  Jay Gray stated the City Council benefits package increases for individuals who have at
  least 10 years of service, inquired as to whether term limit ballot measure options will
  be presented to the voters, and expressed concern regarding limits placed upon
  members of the public as related to participating in ballot measure education efforts
  hosted by the City. Mr. Gray expressed opposition to the City’s Facebook comments
  policy.
 City of Cerritos  Monday, November 15, 2021, 6:30 p.m.
City Council Special Meeting  Page 3 of 4

4.  Review and consideration of the City of Cerritos City Charter (COUNCIL)
  (continued)

  Matt Kauble expressed support for clarity in the drafting of any proposed term limits
  ballot measures and confirmed that any voter-approved changes to term limits would
  not apply retrospectively to any incumbent or former Councilmember.

  Jay Gray inquired as to the benefits package provided to City Council.

  Noting there were no other members of the public who elected to provide public
  comment on City Council term limits or any other matter related to the City Charter, the
  public comments period was closed.

  Councilmember Barrows stated his preference to have any proposed amendments on
  term limits come to the Council through the voter-sponsored initiative process.

  Councilmember Yokoyama requested information related to the fiscal impacts of the
  Charter review process and placement of proposed ballot measures before the voters at
  an authorized election.

  Mayor Hu expressed her support for the current term limit provisions.

  Mayor Pro Tem Vo expressed support for the three lifetime term limit options to enable
  the City, through its elected representatives, to have more influence on regional, state,
  and federal matters which impact the City.

  There was no further Council comment on this matter.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, as related to the
  comprehensive Charter “clean up” (update and modernization) document attached with
  the agenda report submitted for this item:

  1. To direct staff to prepare the proposed Council-initiated ballot question and full text of
  the associated proposed Charter amendment ordinance; and

  2. Place the items for review and consideration on the December 9, 2021 City Council
  regular meeting agenda for potential submission to the voters at the Tuesday, April
  12, 2022 Cerritos General Municipal Election (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

(minutes continue on the next page)

4.  Review and consideration of the City of Cerritos City Charter (COUNCIL)
  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, as related to the proposed
  “anti-nepotism” policy document attached with the agenda report submitted for this item:

  1. To direct staff to prepare the proposed Council-initiated ballot question and full text of
  the associated proposed Charter amendment ordinance; and

  2. Place the items for review and consideration on the December 9, 2021 City Council
  regular meeting agenda for potential submission to the voters at the Tuesday, April
  12, 2022 Cerritos General Municipal Election (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, as related to the following four
  (4) proposed options related to City Council term limits:

  Option 1:  Removal of all term limit provisions
  Option 2:  Keep the current term limit provisions
  Option 3:  Lifetime term limits: 2 full-terms
  Option 4:  Lifetime term limits: 3 full-terms

  1. To direct staff to prepare the proposed Council-initiated ballot question and full text of
  the associated proposed Charter amendment ordinance; and

  2. Place the items for review and consideration on the December 9, 2021 City Council
  regular meeting agenda for potential submission to the voters at the Tuesday, April
  12, 2022 Cerritos General Municipal Election (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

5.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 8:16 p.m.
